index_record.dataset_generation_caption: The figure presents a causal graph for the Non-linear Triangle dataset, as indicated by the caption 'Figure 1: Causal graph for Non-linear Triangle dataset'. The global layout is simple and centered, consisting of three rectangular nodes arranged in a triangular configuration. The node labeled X₀ is positioned at the top center. Below it, to the left, is the node labeled X₁, and to the right, at the same vertical level as X₁, is the node labeled X₂. All nodes are represented as white rectangles with black borders and contain their respective variable labels in black serif font, centered within each box. There are no additional colors or visual embellishments; the entire diagram uses a monochrome scheme with black lines and text on a white background. The connections between the nodes are depicted using solid black arrows, indicating directed causal relationships. Specifically, there is an arrow from X₀ pointing downward to X₁, signifying that X₀ causally influences X₁. Another arrow extends diagonally from X₀ to the right and downward to X₂, indicating a direct causal effect of X₀ on X₂. Additionally, there is a horizontal arrow from X₁ to X₂, showing that X₁ also causally affects X₂. This structure forms a directed acyclic graph (DAG) where X₀ is a common cause of both X₁ and X₂, and X₁ is an intermediate cause of X₂. The graph visually encodes the causal dependencies among the three variables, which are central to understanding the data-generating process in the Non-linear Triangle dataset. No equations or mathematical expressions are included in the diagram itself, but the structure implies underlying non-linear functional relationships consistent with the dataset's name. The overall design is minimalistic and focused solely on representing the causal structure without any extraneous elements.
